cards.headline_target: Class 2 Medicines Recall: Advanz Pharma Limited, Mynzepli 40…

quotes.original: Advanz Pharma Limited are recalling specified batches of Mynzepli 40 mg/mL solution for injection in pre-filled syringe as a precautionary measure.

deterministic_detail.body: DMRC reference number DMRC - 41252013 Marketing Authorisation Holder Advanz Pharma Limited Medicine Details Mynzepli 40 mg/mL solution for injection in pre-filled syringe PL: 56734/0022 Active Ingredient: aflibercept SNOMED code: 45567511000001107 GTIN: 05021691005605 Affected Lot Batch Numbers Batch No. Expiry Date Pack Size First Distributed 2325742 Jun-2027 1 02/01/2026 2325726 May-2027 1 10/10/2025 Background Advanz Pharma Limited are recalling the specified batches of Mynzepli 40 mg/mL solution for injection in pre-filled syringe as a precautionary measure because a small variation in the size of the finger grip could affect how the medicine is administered and potentially pose a risk to patient safety. The finger grip/flange provides a platform/surface for better grip of the syringe. It allows the user to securely hold the pre-filled syringe while applying pressure to the plunger rod during product administration. Advice for Healthcare Professionals: Stop supplying the above batches immediately. Quarantine all remaining stock and return it to your supplier using your supplier’s approved process. Advanz Pharma have confirmed that other unaffected batches of Mynzepli 40 mg/mL solution for injection in pre-filled syringe are currently available for distribution. Advice for Patients: This is a Pharmacy and Wholesaler level recall, therefore no further action is required by patients. This product is only administered by a qualified healthcare professional experienced in administering intravitreal injections. Patients who experience adverse reactions or have any questions about the medication should seek medical attention. Any suspected adverse reactions should also be reported via the MHRA Yellow Card scheme . Additional information: For all enquiries and information on this product, please email medicalinformation@advanzpharma.com , or telephone +44 (0) 208 588 9131. Recipients of this Medicines Recall should bring it to the attention of relevant contacts by copy of this notice. NHS regional teams are asked to forward this to community pharmacists and dispensing general practitioners for information. cards.headline_target: Class 2 Medicines Recall: Accord-UK Ltd, Lercanidipine Hydro…

quotes.original: Accord-UK Ltd is recalling one batch of Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10mg Tablets due to a packaging mix-up involving the incorrect strength.

deterministic_detail.body: DMRC reference number DMRC - 41285957 Marketing Authorisation Holder Accord-UK Ltd Medicine Details Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10mg Film-Coated Tablets PL: 00142/1154 Active Ingredient: lercanidipine hydrochloride SNOMED code: 16607111000001105 GTIN: 05055565768242 Affected Lot Batch Numbers Batch No. Expiry Date Pack Size First Distributed M2510877 11/2028 28 24/06/2026 Background Accord-UK Ltd is recalling one batch of Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10mg Tablets due to a packaging mix-up involving the incorrect strength. One complaint has been received to date, in which a sealed carton of Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10mg Tablets 28 (Batch No. M2510877) was found to contain one blister strip of the correct tablets, and one blister strip of Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 20mg Tablets (Batch No. M2510831). This recall is being conducted at the pharmacy and wholesaler level as Accord-UK Limited has shown that the likelihood of the mix up, and the subsequent risk to patients, is low. If a patient prescribed lercanidipine 10 mg were to inadvertently receive 20 mg daily for approximately two weeks, the anticipated risk would be an exaggerated pharmacological effect; particularly reduction in blood pressure with associated symptoms such as dizziness, headache, flushing, palpitations or symptomatic hypotension. However, 20 mg remains within the authorised therapeutic dose range for routine use of this product. The tablets have distinct colours and the occurrence of the defect is currently anticipated to be very low. Advice for Healthcare Professionals: Stop supplying the above batch immediately. Quarantine all remaining stock and return it to your supplier using your supplier’s approved process. This recall is at the pharmacy and wholesaler level and not directed to patient level as 20 mg remains within the authorised therapeutic dose range for routine use of this product. The tablets have distinct colours and the occurrence of the defect is currently anticipated to be very low. However, should a patient present a pack with the incorrect medicine, pharmacy teams should exercise their professional judgement to supply the correct medication. Advice for Patients: Accord has received a single report of a carton of Accord-UK Ltd Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10 mg Tablets containing a blister strip of Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 20 mg Tablets and are being recalled as a precautionary measure. 20 mg remains within the authorised therapeutic dose range for routine use of this product. The tablets have distinct colours and the occurrence of the defect is currently anticipated to be very low. If you were prescribed Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10 mg Tablets, and received an Accord pack with batch number M2510877, please carefully check the blister strips inside (the batch number and expiry date information can be found on outer carton, see the images in Annex 1). If the carton contains blister strips that are labelled as Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10 mg Tablets, you do not need to take further action and may continue to take the tablets. If the carton contains a blister strip that is labelled as Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 20 mg Tablets, do not take the medicine, contact your pharmacy. If you believe you have taken the Lercanidipine 20 mg Tablets and are currently experiencing any side effects such as dizziness, headache, flushing or palpitations then please seek immediate medical advice. Please take the leaflet that came with your medicine and any remaining tablets with you to your pharmacy or GP practice. If you are unsure or have any questions, please seek advice from your pharmacy or other healthcare professionals involved in your treatment. Patients who experience adverse reactions or have any questions about the medication should seek medical attention. Any suspected adverse reactions should also be reported via the MHRA Yellow Card scheme. Additional information: For all medical information enquiries and information on this product, please email Accord-UK Medical Information Department medinfo@accord-healthcare.com , or telephone 01271 385257. For stock control enquiries please email Accord-UK Customer Services Team customerservices@accord-healthcare.com , or telephone 0800 373573. Recipients of this Medicines Recall should bring it to the attention of relevant contacts by copy of this notice. NHS regional teams are asked to forward this to community pharmacists and dispensing general practitioners for information. Yours faithfully Defective Medicines Report Centre 10 South Colonnade Canary Wharf London E14 4PU Telephone +44 (0)20 3080 6574 DMRC@mhra.gov.uk Download document Class 2 Medicines Recall: Accord-UK Ltd, Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10mg Film-Coated Tablets, EL(26)A/45 Annex 1 Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10mg Tablets – Carton Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10mg Tablets – showing Batch details Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10mg Tablets – Correct blister of 14 tablets BN M2510877 Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 20mg Tablets – Incorrect blister of 14 tablets BN M2510831 Differences in appearance between Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 10mg Tablets and Lercanidipine Hydrochloride 20mg Tablets.

cards.headline_target: Class 2 Medicines Recall: Xeal Pharma, Clopidogrel Oral Liqu…

quotes.original: Xeal Pharma have informed MHRA that all strengths of their Clopidogrel Oral Suspension and Clopidogrel Oral Solution products contain less than the labelled amount of clopidogrel.

deterministic_detail.body: DMRC reference number DMRC - 41238898 Marketing Authorisation Holder Xeal Pharma Medicine Details Clopidogrel Oral Solution, Clopidogrel Oral Suspension Unlicensed medicine (MS 46688) Active Ingredient: clopidogrel hydrogen sulfate SNOMED code: N/A GTIN: N/A Affected Lot Batch Numbers For a list of defected batches, see Annex 1 Background Xeal Pharma have informed MHRA that all strengths of their Clopidogrel Oral Suspension and Clopidogrel Oral Solution products contain less than the labelled amount of clopidogrel. Due to a formulation error, the impacted batches contain 76% of the required amount of clopidogrel. All batches produced prior to this notification are affected. Please note this is a Class 2 Patient, Pharmacy and Wholesaler level recall. Advice for Healthcare Professionals: Stop supplying the above batches immediately. Quarantine all remaining stock and return it to your supplier using your supplier’s approved process. Based on the risk assessment by Xeal Pharma, patient harm is not anticipated in patients receiving the affected product for long-term preventative treatment. However, patients would not receive the full, prescribed dose. Pharmacists should identify and immediately contact all patients who have been dispensed these batches and ask them to confirm if they have remaining stock within their possession. If batch traceability information is not available, all patients dispensed this product from 20 July 2026 should be contacted. Patients should be informed that the product contained a lower dose than prescribed and patients and carers should be reminded that suddenly stopping this medicine may cause serious thrombotic events. If the pharmacist identifies any patients with an impacted product, they should contact the patient’s GP or prescriber and discuss ongoing treatment for the patient. As patients may require monitoring, other clinicians and healthcare professionals may need to be involved. Prescribers, clinicians, and other healthcare professionals involved in the prescribing/monitoring of patients who are using Clopidogrel Oral Solution or Suspension should contact their patients and/or carers directly to ensure that their treatment is reviewed. Healthcare professionals should be aware that there are no licensed clopidogrel oral suspension/solutions available. Patients with impacted batches may require a dose correction, alternative licensed formulations or a different treatment option. Xeal Pharma have confirmed that all future stock will be manufactured with the correct strength and calculations applied. Advice for Patients: Never stop taking medicines such as clopidogrel without medical advice. Suddenly stopping clopidogrel may cause serious thrombotic events. Your GP, specialist, pharmacist, or other healthcare professional will contact you to, where required, make sure you get a new prescription for an alternative product. Once you have a replacement, you should return the impacted product to your pharmacy as part of the recall. You can contact your healthcare professional directly if you are worried, but you should keep taking your medicine as advised until you get an alternative. No reports of patient harm have been received regarding this issue and the recall is being undertaken out of an abundance of caution. Patients who experience adverse reactions or have any questions about the medication should seek medical attention. Any suspected adverse reactions should also be reported via the MHRA Yellow Card scheme . Additional information: For all enquiries and information on this product, please email contact@xealpharma.co.uk , or telephone 0121 3090067. Recipients of this Medicines Recall should bring it to the attention of relevant contacts by copy of this notice. NHS regional teams are asked to forward this to community pharmacists and dispensing general practitioners for information. Yours faithfully Defective Medicines Report Centre 10 South Colonnade Canary Wharf London E14 4PU Telephone +44 (0)20 3080 6574 DMRC@mhra.gov.uk Download document Class 2 Medicines Recall: Xeal Pharma, Clopidogrel Oral Liquids (all strengths), EL(26)A/43
